analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: ON THE MOVE...
key_insights: The week opened with early demand in semis, mostly from the long-only community, then ended in an aggressive sell-off with very little defense on the way down.

Asset managers finished the week net sellers, reversing early-week tech demand. Hedge fund flows finished balanced. Most supply came from tech, and the selling was orderly compared with the prior ~2 weeks.
The size of the moves looked systematic and top-down driven. ETFs were ~31% of the tape, the highest full-session level since June. Month-end flows also contributed.

Consumer outperformed the market on Thursday and Friday. Drivers were rotation out of tech into Staples, better earnings in restaurants (CMG, WING, EAT) and cruise lines (NCLH, RCL), and covering in under-owned names (CROX, BOOT).
Key S&P levels the desk is watching are the 100-day moving average at 7614 and the CTA medium-term threshold at 7554, where most of the notional sits.

Per the Prime weekly (as of the Oct 29 close), US fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 0.1 pts to 216.3% (66th percentile over one year). Net leverage rose 3.6 pts to 47%, which is the 7th percentile over one year.
Hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in 4 weeks, driven by short covers in macro products and, to a lesser extent, single stocks.

Info Tech was the most net bought sector through Thursday but is still heavily net sold month-to-date in October. Megacap tech was net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions, which the desk reads as little recovery in risk appetite.

Mid-day performance estimates (as of 1PM EST) showed global fundamental L/S managers down 1.2% (-1.8 SD), led by beta and Info Tech. TMT-focused funds were down 3.8% (-2.6 SD) and 12.6% month-to-date, which cut their YTD gain to +5.1%.
Next week is the last major week of Q3 earnings, with AAPL on Monday as the tech standout. Attention then shifts to the US midterm elections on Tuesday and the jobs report on Friday.
The Wednesday QRA tenor details will be watched for any change to issuance or supply, with the focus on the back end and specifically 20y and 30y.
earnings_insights: Restaurants (CMG, WING, EAT) and cruise lines (NCLH, RCL) reported better earnings that supported consumer outperformance on Thursday and Friday. No figures are given.
AAPL reports Monday and is flagged as the tech standout in the last major week of Q3 earnings.
